findings.summary: A flagged item that is passed over stays queued with no pause, so each later batch gives it two more paid attempts until the scope guard escalates to a pause or the flag stops holding.
findings.evidence: ItemEnd::Flagged only calls pass_over. The new test asserts `queued == ["a"]`, and the CHANGELOG says 'Nothing is written'. The accepted reading chose this ('it does not write a new pause file'), so it is not a mismatch. Still, a person may want the next batch to skip an item that already failed twice on a flagged line.

findings.summary: Athena::line_flag repeats the line-lookup steps of Athena::line_pause; the two could share a helper.
findings.evidence: Lines 799-803 are the same as lines 785-789 in line_pause; only the mark path, the filter and the level test differ.

summary: The change does what was asked. Before it, after an item's second failure the drain asked only whether the item's line was paused, because `Athena::line_pause` returns pauses only, so an item on a flagged line ended the batch with a repeated-failure stop. Now `Drain::attempts` makes a second check at that point: it asks a new `Steps::flagged`, which `RealSteps` backs with a new `Athena::line_flag`. That returns the stored flag only while the line's records still reach a flag, which matches how `live_marks` decides it. If the line is flagged, the item is passed over with one line giving the flag signals and reason, and the next item runs. An item on a line with no flag and no pause still stops the batch. I ran `cargo test -p athena-cli --test drain` in this snapshot and all 164 tests passed, including the three new ones and every existing paused-line test. The new `scope_guard` unit test also passes. Athena's recorded checks for this commit show fmt, clippy and `cargo test --locked` clean. The docs, the stop-reasons help text and CHANGELOG.md all state the new rule. All five changed files are on the deliverables list. I found one minor point: no pause file is written, so a later batch will give a still-flagged item two more paid attempts. The accepted reading chose this, and it is worth deciding on later.
